# Native Moving-Path Force and Length Consistency

F07 child #11856 isolates a native path-work discrepancy found during #11834.
This original fixture and its diagnostic gate establish implementation facts
only. They do not qualify donor anatomy, physiological force capacity, muscle
fitting, capture reconstruction, or independent full-state muscle replay.

## Original Mechanism and Units

The executable reference is `scripts/diagnostics/native_path_work.py`. It creates
one body of mass 1 kg, centre of mass at its pin, and isotropic inertia
$I=0.02\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2}$. The pin rotates about the world $z$ axis. Gravity is
zero. One native `PathActuator` has optimal force 1 N and receives native control
1, with no controller, contact, coupler, wrapping surface, or donor resource.

The ground point is $(-0.2,0.2,0)$ m. The body-local via point is
$(0.1+0.03q,0.05,0)$ m and the insertion is $(0.2,0.05,0)$ m. A fixed-point
control replaces the via point with $(0.1,0.05,0)$ m. These are original
diagnostic dimensions, not anatomical estimates. Both terminal points share
the same body. The moving-point coordinate sockets all reference the pin;
the $y$ and $z$ functions are constant.

For the tested $q\in\{-0.2,0,0.2\}$ rad, the terminal segment has length
$l_s=0.1-0.03q$ m and therefore $-dl_s/dq=0.03$ m/rad. There is no singular
segment, clamp, or assembly constraint in this interval. No extrapolation
outside this interval or physiological coordinate-domain claim is made.

## Native Force, Geometry, and Numerical Check

The assay reloads each serialized original model and copies its native initial
state for each independent sample. At zero speed, native unit-tension
acceleration gives the generalized force $Q=I\ddot q$. Separately, at unit
speed, native path lengthening gives $\dot l$. Under the additional assumption
of a workless path transmission, the expected identities are

$$
r=-\frac{\partial l}{\partial q},\qquad Q=T r,\qquad
Q\dot q=-T\dot l.
$$

This assumption is not automatic for a `MovingPathPoint`.
[Sherman, Seth and Delp (2013)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4404026/)
define moment arm from force effectiveness and explain that moving path points
can introduce unaccounted guide work. Equality with tendon excursion requires
workless constraints. The [official FunctionBasedPath reference](https://opensim-org.github.io/opensim-moco-site/docs/1.3.0/html_user/classOpenSim_1_1FunctionBasedPath.html)
repeats this caveat. Therefore the following discrepancy does not, by itself,
prove an OpenSim runtime defect or an erroneous force-defined moment arm.

The existing public `compute_path_length_finite_difference_moment_arm` and
`validate_moment_arm_consistency` providers are reused. Central stencils use
$h\in\{10^{-3},10^{-4},10^{-5}\}$ rad; achieved coordinate spans are recorded.
The 1e-7 m consistency threshold is a numerical diagnostic threshold, not a
measured physiological or instrument uncertainty. Coarse fixed-path stencil
error is about 1e-8 m and decreases on refinement. Finest-stencil tests require
the fixed discrepancy and moving discrepancy minus 0.03 m to be below 1e-10 m.

On OpenSim `4.6-2026-06-22-85aaf64`, all nine fixed-path samples pass and all
nine moving-path samples fail the workless-identity gate. At $q=0$ the moving case
has native moment arm 0.06260990337 m, native $\ddot q=3.1304951685$
rad/s² under 1 N tension, but full geometric derivative moment arm
0.09260990337 m. Native lengthening speed is -0.09260990337 m/s at unit
coordinate speed. The 0.03 m discrepancy agrees with the terminal segment
derivative and persists across step refinement. Actual applied-force dynamics
therefore agree with the native moment arm. The difference from the full
length derivative is a guide-work accounting question. At unit tension and
unit coordinate speed, $-T\dot l-Q\dot q=0.03$ W in this fixture. This residual
does not identify a physical guide mechanism or authorize adding a correction
torque. Preserve the force-defined native moment arm and qualify the guide-work
semantics separately.

Nonfinite moment arms, sampled lengths, coordinates, steps, tolerances and
derivative results are rejected. Unresolvable stencils and nonpositive
tolerances are rejected. These checks use explicit exceptions so disabling
optional `DBC_LEVEL` diagnostics cannot admit invalid scientific evidence.
The driver always emits `scientific_status="unqualified"`, including for the
fixed control; sample agreement cannot qualify a whole model or replay.

## Source and Runtime Identity

The reviewed official source revision is
`85aaf6450a2f22457dac4d1ab35adfed9d3a8e43`:

- [GeometryPath.cpp](https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/blob/85aaf6450a2f22457dac4d1ab35adfed9d3a8e43/OpenSim/Simulation/Model/GeometryPath.cpp):
  SHA-256 `dbb13642bb2db9a46e6cc02653692f20e414d1a69f521ea106ecfd5bd2ccced5`.
- [MomentArmSolver.cpp](https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/blob/85aaf6450a2f22457dac4d1ab35adfed9d3a8e43/OpenSim/Simulation/MomentArmSolver.cpp):
  SHA-256 `42b6614770f04354b597fecfa8c166a6c4b3e2d9a72cd780682bbad1a0c40ad3`.

In that source, `GeometryPath::produceForces` applies moving-point generalized
work inside the condition that the next path point belongs to a different
mobilized body. Its length calculation includes same-body segments.
`MomentArmSolver` obtains unit-tension path forces and projects generalized
force through the coordinate coupling vector. This source structure explains
the observed partition in this source version. Historical moving-guide semantics
and the force definition must be reviewed before diagnosing a runtime defect;
no runtime patch is included.

Receipts record actual native version, Python version, loaded extension
hashes, original XML hashes, native loaded serialization hashes, numerical
settings, probe and gate-provider hashes, and unchanged source/loaded-model
checks. The reviewed source pin is distinguished from the executing binary:
source-to-binary reproducibility and complete dependent-DLL closure remain
explicitly unverified. Missing verification is never a zero or a pass.

## Reproduction and Follow-Up Gates

From the repository root, with the actual native provider selected:

```powershell
& C:/Users/diete/Repositories/.venv-feedback-opensim/Scripts/python.exe -m scripts.diagnostics.native_path_work --output C:/Users/diete/Repositories/docs/development/feedback_controls_planning/native_model_evaluation/original_path_work_11856_semantics_revision
& C:/Users/diete/Repositories/.venv-feedback-opensim/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/opensim/test_native_path_work.py -o addopts='' -q
python3 -m scripts.check_design_manual_governance
```

The output contains only original fixtures and observations. It does not
download or redistribute donor assets. Native tests skip explicitly without
the bindings; skipped tests cannot substantiate a native result.

Before choosing a model, first decide whether workless transmission is justified
or an explicit guide-work/power budget and physical interpretation are required.
The equality gate applies only to the former. A defensible guide-work model
with independently declared bounds may support model qualification; an
unexplained residual cannot silently pass as ordinary muscle-to-skeleton work.
Alternative paths or native changes remain separate reviewed options, with
independent source, anatomical and calibration evidence. Replacing native
moment arms by geometric gradients in an optimizer without changing and
validating the actual force plant would create a different model and would
not resolve replay consistency. Removing the terminal segment, freezing the
moving point, or altering donor couplers to hide the failure is inadmissible.
Any native patch needs independent regression, exact runtime provenance,
power/force checks and review before donor reuse. No third-party outreach is
part of this child. The donor ECRL wrapping discrepancy, anatomical input
bounds, notice conditions, grip/contact, force capacity and full-capture
full-state replay remain open. The existing milestone DAG and model parity
denominator are unchanged. Manual release remains blocked.
